text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Workers at the state-run Tarom SA airline threaten to launch strike and block runways, to protest against Tarom's plans to cut 1,000 jobs.
- The leftist opposition will present parliament a non-confidence motion in the centrist government on Tuesday.
- Some five million hectares of cropland are affected by weeds, the paper says.
- Bucharest mayor Viorel Lis plans to open a free-trade zone near the capital city, the paper says.
- The Daewoo Automobile SA car maker in Craiova opened a factory for engines and gear boxes.
- Some 80 percent of Romania's small and medium-sized companies are almost banckrupt, the paper quotes the chairman of the National employers union, Stefan Chelariu, as saying.
- Tarom's 1996 losses amounted to $24 million, the paper said.
- The World Bank will discuss new loans for Romania on Tuesday.
